c.tagline: Zimbabwe's second city of wide colonial avenues and Matobo's granite hills.

taxi.fareNote: Shared minibuses (combis) run fixed routes for small change; metered taxis are rare, so agree a fare before you get in and ride-hailing apps are not established here. Prices are in US dollars; the local ZiG is legal tender too but change often comes back in USD.

emergency.note: 999 is the general emergency line, 995 reaches police and 994 the ambulance service; response can be slow, so private medical-evacuation providers are widely used. 112 also works from mobiles.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

solo.f: generally fine; avoid walking after dark

hood_landmark.Suburbs: Natural History Museum of Zimbabwe, Bulawayo

avoid.reason: No strict no-go zones, but skip the high-density western townships after dark unless accompanied by a local.
Pickpockets and phone-snatchers work the city centre and bus ranks; keep valuables out of sight.

hood_desc: The grid of wide, tree-lined colonial avenues at the heart of town, with City Hall, markets, shops and most budget hotels; walkable and central, the easiest base for first-timers.
A leafy older residential area just east of the CBD (its actual name), full of jacaranda-lined streets, guesthouses and the Natural History Museum nearby; calm and green yet close in.
A quiet, leafy suburb a five-minute drive from the centre with B&Bs, lodges and gardens; relaxed and residential, popular with families and longer-stay visitors.
One of Bulawayo's most exclusive suburbs of large homes on tree-lined streets a few kilometres from the CBD; upscale, spacious and tranquil.
Bulawayo's oldest township, a birthplace of Zimbabwean music and nationalist history and home to the lively Makokoba (Sixth Avenue) market; rich in culture though rough around the edges.

water.note: Chronic shortages and aging pipes make bottled or filtered water the safe choice.

transit.hours: Combis run roughly dawn to early evening; after dark the options thin out and a booked taxi is the safest choice.
transit.note: Bulawayo has no metro, tram or formal city bus network. Shared minibuses (combis, or 'emergency taxis') cover the main routes from the city-centre ranks, supplemented by private taxis.
transit.pay: Fares are paid in cash to the conductor, usually in small US-dollar notes; the local ZiG is also accepted. There is no transit card.

bus: Long-distance coaches to Harare, Victoria Falls and Johannesburg (Intercape, Pathfinder, CityLink)
Shared combis to Matobo, Gwanda and regional towns
train: Overnight National Railways of Zimbabwe sleeper train to Victoria Falls; a slow line also runs to Harare

transit.m: Taxi or hotel shuttle to the city centre (25-30 min); there is no scheduled airport bus

tip.r: ~10% at restaurants; small change for guides and drivers is appreciated.
